From e2bb9fab08cbcc7922050c7eb0bd650807abfa4e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Kan Liang <kan.liang@linux.intel.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2021 08:32:38 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] perf/x86/intel/uncore: Fix invalid unit check

The uncore unit with the type ID 0 and the unit ID 0 is missed.

The table3 of the uncore unit maybe 0. The
uncore_discovery_invalid_unit() mistakenly treated it as an invalid
value.

Remove the !unit.table3 check.

Fixes: edae1f06c2cd ("perf/x86/intel/uncore: Parse uncore discovery tables")
Signed-off-by: Kan Liang <kan.liang@linux.intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Reviewed-by: Andi Kleen <ak@linux.intel.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/1629991963-102621-3-git-send-email-kan.liang@linux.intel.com

diff --git a/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_discovery.h b/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_discovery.h
index 7280c8a3c831..6d735611c281 100644
--- a/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_discovery.h
+++ b/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_discovery.h
@@ -30,7 +30,7 @@
 
 
 #define uncore_discovery_invalid_unit(unit)			\
-	(!unit.table1 || !unit.ctl || !unit.table3 ||	\
+	(!unit.table1 || !unit.ctl || \
 	 unit.table1 == -1ULL || unit.ctl == -1ULL ||	\
 	 unit.table3 == -1ULL)
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_discovery.h`**
   - The macro `uncore_discovery_invalid_unit(unit)` was modified by removing the check for `!unit.table3`. 
   - The updated macro now only checks for `!unit.table1`, `!unit.ctl`, and the conditions where `unit.table1`, `unit.ctl`, or `unit.table3` are equal to `-1ULL`.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification addresses a bug where the uncore unit with type ID 0 and unit ID 0 was incorrectly treated as invalid due to the presence of the `!unit.table3` check. By removing this check, the code now correctly allows for the possibility that `table3` can be 0, thus fixing the invalid unit detection logic. This change is directly related to the bug fix mentioned in the patch description, which aims to improve the handling of uncore unit discovery.

Here is the commit message:
perf/x86/intel/uncore: Fix invalid unit check

The uncore unit with the type ID 0 and the unit ID 0 is missed.

The table3 of the uncore unit maybe 0. The
uncore_discovery_invalid_unit() mistakenly treated it as an invalid
value.

Remove the !unit.table3 check.

Fixes: edae1f06c2cd ("perf/x86/intel/uncore: Parse uncore discovery tables")
Signed-off-by: Kan Liang <kan.liang@linux.intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Reviewed-by: Andi Kleen <ak@linux.intel.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/1629991963-102621-3-git-send-email-kan.liang@linux.intel.com

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the incorrect assumption that a `table3` value of 0 indicates an invalid uncore unit. The check for `!unit.table3` in the `uncore_discovery_invalid_unit` macro mistakenly treated a valid unit with `table3` equal to 0 as invalid, leading to erroneous behavior in uncore unit discovery.

Here is the patch:
 
 #define uncore_discovery_invalid_unit(unit)			\
-	(!unit.table1 || !unit.ctl || !unit.table3 ||	\
+	(!unit.table1 || !unit.ctl || \
 	 unit.table1 == -1ULL || unit.ctl == -1ULL ||	\
 	 unit.table3 == -1ULL)

```c

```
Reason:
The check for `!unit.table3` incorrectly assumes that a `table3` value of 0 is invalid. This leads to valid uncore units being mistakenly identified as invalid, causing issues in the uncore unit discovery process.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
// Removed the check for !unit.table3
```
Reason:
By removing the `!unit.table3` check, the code no longer treats a `table3` value of 0 as invalid. This allows valid uncore units with `table3` equal to 0 to be correctly recognized, thus fixing the erroneous behavior in uncore unit discovery.
